references.text: The parable of the vineyard in Isaiah 5:1-7 has similarities with the parable Jesus tells in Mark 12:6, where a vineyard and its owner also play central roles.
Psalm 118:22-23 about the stone the builders rejected which became the cornerstone can be seen in light of Jesus as the beloved son who is sent last and rejected in Mark 12:6.
Hosea 6:6, where God expresses a desire for mercy rather than sacrifice, can be related to God sending his beloved son in Mark 12:6 as an expression of His ultimate mercy.
The parable of the vineyard in Matthew 21:33-46 is parallel to Mark 12:6, focusing on the beloved son who is sent last and mistreated.
The parable of the vineyard in Luke 20:9-19 is another parallel account to Mark 12:6, where the beloved son is sent last and killed.
Hebrews 1:1-2 speaks of God who in these last days has spoken to us through the Son, which can be seen in connection with the beloved son sent last in Mark 12:6.
